item.title: J.B. Hunt CEO: We’re being careful pushing price
item.description: Shelley Simpson and her team see signs that the market is tightening but say most customers think the shift is temporary or seasonal. Capex at the No. 4 carrier on the FleetOwner 500 could rise by $225 million this year.

item.title: How emotions can help trucking professionals retain important information and improve focus
item.description: Digital overload can harm memory and focus, making emotional engagement key for effective learning.

item.title: Next-gen fleet safety tech: A headrest that scans drivers' brains
item.description: A tech company's new contactless brainwave sensor can detect drivers' fatigue and distraction. When the sensor reaches fleets, it could provide early warnings before physical signs of fatigue manifest.

item.title: Dry van and reefer spot rates slide as flatbed prices climb, FTR and DAT report
item.description: Spot market data shows dry van and reefer rates sliding fast, while flatbed pricing continues to gain ground.

item.title: Roeth: Fleets focus on trailer aerodynamics to maximize tractor-trailer fuel economy
item.description: NACFE data shows trailer aerodynamics is the most downloaded topic, reflecting fleets’ focus on real fuel efficiency gains.

item.title: Paccar international EVP Mike Dozier to retire in April
item.description: The executive vice president responsibilities of Mike Dozier, who spent 37 years with the parent company of Kenworth and Peterbilt, will be divided between two leaders.

item.title: 2026 Outlook: Rise of AI, dwindling EV focus, and brain-reading trucks
item.description: The first roundtable of 2026 looks at the start of this year: carrier bankruptcies, regulatory crackdowns, emerging technologies, and hopes for that market upturn to finally arrive.

item.title: Diesel prices rise across the U.S., reaching $3.53 per gallon in January
item.description: Gas and diesel prices rise this week, with Gulf Coast diesel and Rocky Mountain gasoline seeing the largest regional increases.

item.title: Trailer orders surge to two-year high, but market headwinds push volatility into 2026
item.description: Led by dry vans, deferred fleet plans drive 2025 trailer order surge; yet manufacturer production fell to its lowest levels in 15 years as carriers embark on another year potentially defined by trade, tariffs, and rising costs.

item.title: Trucking capacity reached a bottom; 2026 just needs better freight demand
item.description: For-hire capacity has shrunk to "almost as deep as it can without the loss of a lot of carriers," FTR's Avery Vise says. If freight demand picks up midyear, sustained rate increases could finally be in sight.
